title: Canonical derived module calculus on algebraic spaces
statement: For an algebraic space X over a scheme S [def-trf-algebraic-space], use the small ringed model and its specified restriction equivalence [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define D(O_X) using this equivalent small ringed model, with arbitrary localization morphism universe w. Define D_QCoh as the full subcategory whose cohomology, transported back along the module equivalence, is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The structure sheaf in degree zero belongs to D_QCoh. For a morphism f, conjugate the canonical compatible-chart direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] by the two module equivalences and take its unbounded right derived functor. The conjugated functor is additive and these module categories have K-injective resolutions, so this is computed by K-injectives. A QCoh direct-image presentation is a functor on these full subcategories with a natural isomorphism to this fixed ambient Rf_*. For each etale scheme chart, compose the inverse model equivalence with restriction to Zariski opens [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]; this is additive, and its right derived functor is the derived chart restriction, allowing an independent localization universe for the scheme. For maps to a scheme represented as an algebraic space by its representable sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], define the chart structure morphism by Yoneda preimage. The internal derived Hom is the existing K-injective Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the equivalent small site. Use the normalized closed tensor-Hom and ordinary-unit model [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] to define the scalar endomorphism map as the transpose of O_X tensor K to K. No invertibility or perfection is imposed by these definitions.

proof.text: Compute the cohomology of the degree-zero structure sheaf using the single-functor homology isomorphism in degree zero and the vanishing of single-complex homology in every other degree. The small-module restriction takes the original structure module to the small structure module, so the equivalence unit identifies its inverse image with the original unit. On every original chart, present this unit by one generator and no relations. Present any zero module by empty generators and empty relations; the source free module is zero by its free-Hom universal property, so the kernel is zero. These presentations prove quasi-coherence, including on the empty space.

The inverse small-model equivalence preserves binary products and zero maps and hence is additive. The original module direct image is a right adjoint, so it too preserves binary products and zero maps and is additive. Small-model restriction acts sectionwise on morphisms, hence preserves sums definitionally. Their composite is additive.

Apply the existing proved SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian theorem to the actual small-model ring sheaf. The site, ring sections, and module carriers all lie in universe u, as required by that theorem. Apply the Grothendieck-abelian K-injective-resolution theorem [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective].

Zariski scheme-chart restriction is the existing continuous pushforward of module sheaves. Its action on morphisms is sectionwise, so preservation of addition is definitional. Compose it with the additive inverse small-model equivalence. The resulting additivity is the required smallSchemeRestriction_additive instance.
